nodes.title: Imaginary dual and Fourier normalization
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra g, let g^w = Hom_R(g,iR). Set fhat(xi)=integral f(x) exp(xi(x)) dx and a-vee(x)=integral a(xi) exp(-xi(x)) dxi, with Fourier-dual measures. Choose an even real cutoff 0<=chi<=1, equal to one near zero, inside an exponential chart; dg(exp x)=j(x)dx and j(0)=1. Identify xi(x)=2 pi i <eta,x> to compare this forward transform with Mathlib inverse Fourier transform.
proofSteps: Transport the existing Schwartz Fourier equivalence through the imaginary-dual identification and the chosen dual measures.
Normalize the exponential Jacobian at zero; record the exact group-density conversion rather than absorbing it into the symbol.

nodes.title: Nelson Laplacian theorem
nodes.statement: For a strongly continuous unitary representation of a finite-dimensional Lie group, Delta=1-sum dPi(X)^2 on smooth vectors is essentially self-adjoint, its closure is >=1, ||Delta^-1||<=1, and the smooth vectors are the intersection of the domains of all positive integral powers of Delta.
proofSteps: Use the cited essential self-adjointness theorem for the sum of squares and the smooth-vector domain theorem.
The quadratic form is ||v||^2+sum ||dPi(X)v||^2; the spectral lower bound gives the inverse estimate.
acceptance: Check the trivial representation gives Delta=1, then verify the essential-domain assertion before completing any Sobolev scale.

nodes.title: Representation Sobolev scale
nodes.statement: For every integer s, Pi^s is the Hilbert completion of Pi-infinity in ||v||_s=||Delta^(s/2)v||. A word of length r acts Pi^s to Pi^(s-r) with constants depending on the fixed Lie data, not Pi.
proofSteps: Apply spectral calculus to the positive closure of Delta.
Compare integral powers with sums of squared word derivatives, using commutator induction and the domain theorem; complete and dualize.

nodes.title: Commutator operator classes
nodes.statement: For integral order m, an operator T from Pi-infinity to Pi-minus-infinity lies in Psi^m if every iterated commutator theta_(X1...Xr)(T) extends boundedly Pi^s to Pi^(s-m) for all integers s and words. The topology uses these operator norms. Define Psi-minus-infinity as the intersection over integral m and Psi-infinity as the union. For 0<=delta<1, define family Psi_delta^m by uniform boundedness of h^(delta r) times each such commutator norm, with arbitrary Pi(h); h-infinity Psi-minus-infinity means every power of h in every smoothing seminorm.
proofSteps: Use the compatible Sobolev extensions to define the locally convex spaces and topology.
Track the number of commutators in each seminorm to compare uniform families; a continuous seminorm uses finitely many commutator norms and loses only a finite power of h.
acceptance: Verify every listed API law and run the discriminating examples below, including: A bounded operator on L2 need not preserve all Sobolev spaces or have bounded commutators, so boundedness alone does not define Psi^0.

nodes.title: Representation quantization
nodes.statement: For Schwartz a define Op(a,chi)=integral_g chi(x)a-vee(x) Pi(exp x) dx, weakly on the Hilbert representation. Its adjoint is Op(conj a,chi); exact conjugation transports both a and chi.

Use exponential inversion and even real chi for the adjoint; change variables under Ad(g), transforming the dual measure and cutoff together.
Extend compactly supported distributions against smooth matrix coefficients; compatibility on Schwartz symbols follows by density.

nodes.title: Nonstationary phase and BCH Taylor remainder
nodes.statement: For an imaginary smooth phase phi on a fixed open set with |grad phi|>=epsilon>0 and bounded required derivatives near the compact amplitude support, integral f exp(t phi) is O(t^-N sum_(|alpha|<=N)||partial^alpha f||_1), with constants controlled by those bounds. For the BCH phase Omega, all fixed zeta derivatives of Omega-sum_(j<J)Omega_j are O(rho^J), rho=max(|x|,|y|,|x||y||zeta|), on the fixed chart, with the polynomial large-rho bounds used when rho>=1. In the mixed-subalgebra setting g1+g2=g, put B(x,y)=BCH(x,y)-x-y and F(xi,eta,zeta)=integral chi1(x)chi2(y) exp(xi(x)+eta(y)+zeta(B(x,y))) dx dy. Choose the cutoffs sufficiently close to zero and compatible dual norms. For every N>=0 and zeta multi-index gamma, ||(xi,eta)||>=|zeta|/2 implies |partial_zeta^gamma F|<=C_(N,gamma)<(xi,eta)>^-N, uniformly in all three parameters.
proofSteps: For small rho use the graded Taylor formula and the paired vanishing of BCH; split large rho before using polynomial estimates.
Use the integration-by-parts vector field t^-1 |grad phi|^-2 sum conjugate(partial_j phi) partial_j, which acts on exp(t phi) as identity.
Iterate its formal adjoint; bound amplitude derivatives and coefficient derivatives uniformly.

For the F estimate normalize by t=||(xi,eta)||. The linear part of the phase has unit gradient; the BCH correction has small derivative when |zeta|<=2t and the chart is small. Apply the nonstationary estimate for t>=1 and the compact-amplitude estimate for t<=1.
acceptance: Check the integration-by-parts operator reproduces the exponential with the chosen imaginary phase; include derivatives of its coefficients and separate rho<1 from rho>=1.

nodes.title: Localized star remainder bounds
nodes.statement: Let g1+g2=g, 0<=delta1,delta2<1 and delta1+delta2<1. Let a in S_delta1^0(g1*) and b in S_delta2^0(g2*) be localized at omega1 and omega2. For each N>=0 and output multi-index gamma, choose J and M sufficiently large in terms of these fixed data. The remainder r=a star_h b-sum_(j<J) h^j C_j(a,b) satisfies |partial^gamma r(zeta)|<=C h^N <zeta>^-N <omega1>^M <omega2>^M. If g1=g replace the second weight by <omega2>^-N; if g2=g replace the first weight by <omega1>^-N; if both equal g both weights are negative powers. Constants use finitely many bounded localized input seminorms and are independent of h, zeta and the centers. General input orders are restored by the partition weights.
proofSteps: Insert the localized Fourier formulas and treat the four full-algebra versus proper-subalgebra cases of Proposition 7.13 separately.
For comparable centers use the Taylor remainder, spending derivative losses h^-delta1 and h^-delta2.
For separated centers use nonstationary phase with the full-algebra hypotheses required for each negative center weight; proper-subalgebra inputs retain the stated polynomial weights.

For Theorem 7.4, sum case (d) for two full algebras. In the full/proper cases use the negative order required on the full-algebra input to absorb its remaining polynomial center weight. For two proper algebras both orders are minus-infinity, so choose each order sufficiently negative to sum the two polynomial weights from case (a).

nodes.title: Disjoint-spectrum stability
nodes.statement: For the orthogonal or unitary GGP Lie-algebra pair over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, an element x in g* is stable for H (closed orbit and finite isotropy) iff its invariant spectral data and those of x|h have disjoint eigenvalue sets ev(x) and ev(x|h). nodes.title: Smooth period Parseval and weak Weyl bound
nodes.statement: For a smoothing operator T in Psi-minus-infinity, integral_[H][T]=sum_Sigma P_Sigma(T), with absolute convergence and compatibility with smooth differentiation at the fixed auxiliary level. The number of Sigma contributing nonzero periods with |lambda_sigma|<=x is O((1+x)^C) for a group- and level-dependent C. Positivity gives monotone summation for positive T; general smoothing T uses the smooth two-variable kernel and its spectral expansion.
proofSteps: Use compact-quotient automorphic spectral decomposition, elliptic Sobolev bounds and a polynomial eigenvalue-counting estimate supplied by AS.4.
Apply Parseval to each rank-one restricted vector and then sum the auxiliary finite family.

Use the smooth two-variable kernel supplied for Psi-minus-infinity and sufficiently high elliptic Sobolev powers to dominate its spectral tail uniformly, extending from finite rank to smoothing operators. Smoothness of only the diagonal for a smoothly trace-class operator is not this kernel assertion.
acceptance: Count spectral multiplicity and prove the polynomial bound at the fixed auxiliary level. For positive finite-rank T compare directly with Parseval on each restricted vector before extending by trace estimates.

nodes.title: Microlocal period truncation
nodes.statement: Let W be an open subset of h* and U an open quotient subset containing its parameter image as in §29. Let all compactly supported symbols lie over W. Call sigma good if h lambda_sigma lies in U and either sigma is nontempered or h O_sigma meets W. Then integral_[H][a1...ak]=lim_(h to 0) h^d sum_(Sigma with good sigma) P_Sigma(Op_h(a1)...Op_h(ak)). The sum includes multiplicity and the fixed auxiliary factor. Discarded large-parameter terms and tempered orbit-missing terms each have vanishing total contribution.
proofSteps: Choose a relatively compact open U0 inside U containing the invariant-parameter image of the projected compact symbol supports. Outside U0, apply joint localization with arbitrarily strong spectral decay and sum using the weak Weyl bound. This first truncation is valid even when the stated U is unbounded.
For a tempered orbit missing W choose b=1 on the projected symbol support and supported in W; factor the relative operator through sigma quantizations.
Use |tr(T1 T2)|^2<=tr(T1* T1)tr(T2* T2), with the first trace negligible by the orbit trace formula and the second polynomially bounded.

Inside U0 the weak Weyl bound gives only polynomially many terms in h^-1. Sum the orbit-missing estimates after choosing the h-gain larger than that exponent and take the limit-state subsequence. The terms in U outside U0 were already controlled by spectral decay.
acceptance: Treat the large-parameter tail and the tempered orbit-missing tail separately. In Hilbert-Schmidt Cauchy-Schwarz the negligible first factor is tr(T1* T1), never tr(T1* T2).

nodes.statement: Under all corrected global-equidistribution hypotheses, fix k in Cc-infinity([h*] intersect image(O_stable)) and an auxiliary weight k-prime: a finite linear combination of products of finitely supported weights at compact archimedean factors and allowable continuous weights at finite places in R minus q. proofSteps: Choose V,W,U by the stable-neighborhood theorem, so that the truncated good tempered family is exactly the required orbit-distinguished family on the symbol support.
Reduce by linearity to nonnegative product weights. Use positive archimedean inverse branching and the two auxiliary allowability clauses to build tensor-product tests and trace-small majorants.
Apply period Parseval, microlocal truncation and limit-state equidistribution; the limiting main mass is the normalized affine integral times the auxiliary Plancherel mass.
Control the nontempered terms by the small-mass irregular-symbol test and the all-unitary auxiliary majorants; sum residual O(h^N) terms with the weak Weyl bound.
Let the approximation tolerance tend to zero after h. Every subsequence has a further subsequence with the same limit, giving full-sequence convergence.

nodes.title: Stable neighborhoods for spectral truncation
nodes.statement: For nonnegative k compactly supported in the quotient image of O_stable and a regular multiorbit limit h O_Pi to O, choose precompact open V in g^w, W in h^w and U in [h^w]. The closure of V is stable; supp k is contained in the interior of the quotient image of V, the closure of res(V) is contained in W, the quotient image of the closure of W is contained in U, and the closure of U is contained in the quotient image of O_stable. For all sufficiently small h, every tempered sigma with O_(Pi,sigma) empty has h O_sigma disjoint from W. Thus the good tempered summands selected by W are orbit-distinguished.
proofSteps: Cover a compact set of stable limit-orbit points whose quotient image covers supp k. At each point stability makes restriction from the ambient G-orbit to h^w a submersion.
Use the regular-orbit convergence criterion to choose nearby points in h O_Pi for every sufficiently small h, and the submersion theorem to obtain uniform restriction-image neighborhoods.

Choose nested finite unions of these neighborhoods and their quotient images, with all indicated closures inside the next open set. Any h O_sigma meeting W then lies over a point obtained from h O_Pi, so its relative intersection is nonempty.
acceptance: Prove the restriction differential is onto at stable limit points and the image neighborhoods persist uniformly in h. Check the closures are nested in their stated ambient spaces; the source's shorthand is not transitive.
